content.title: About
content.content: Ground flaxseed is milled seeds of the flax plant (Linum usitatissimum). The seeds are rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, dietary fiber, and lignans. The ground form is convenient for adding to oatmeal, smoothies, baked goods, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flax is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown by humans for more than 6,000 years.
Ground flax retains more nutrients than whole seeds because the nutrients are more bioavailable.
Flaxseed is a plant source of alpha‑linolenic acid (ALA), a precursor of omega‑3 fatty acids.
The seeds can be pressed to produce flax oil, used in cooking and cosmetics.
Flax belongs to the Linaceae family and produces small blue‑green flowers.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Ground flaxseed provides alpha‑linolenic acid, which supports heart and vascular health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Lignans – antioxidants
items.content: Lignans have phytoestrogenic and antioxidant properties that may support hormonal balance.

items.title: Supports skin and hair health
items.content: The fatty acids and lignans help moisturize skin and strengthen hair.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Soluble fiber in flax can help reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to flaxseed.

items.title: Cyanogenic glycosides
items.content: Raw whole flaxseeds contain small amounts of cyanogenic compounds; ground flax is generally safe, but it should be stored cold and not consumed in very large amounts without processing.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Fiber can reduce the absorption of certain drugs, so take medications 1–2 hours before or after consuming flax.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add ground flax to oatmeal, yogurt, smoothies, bread, pancakes, and cookies. It can also be sprinkled on salads or used as a thickener in sauces. For optimal absorption, mix with liquid and let it sit a few minutes before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground flaxseed in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. At room temperature it quickly loses aroma and can become rancid.
